case_title: Raju @ Devendra Choubey v. State of Chhattisgarh
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (step mother-in-law) for accused no. 1, with prior domestic dispute; no evidence of prior animosity for accused nos. 2 and 4
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 read with s.34 and s.120B (printed as '1208' in the judgment)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (child witness PW-21); recovery (knife, hair from deceased's grip, bloodstained cloth); medical (post-mortem); test identification parade and in-court identification
aggravating_circumstances: Killing by paid contract killers with a single mission to kill; numerous incised wounds (14) on the victim; victim was two months pregnant
trial_court_outcome: All accused convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 and s.120B IPC; life imprisonment and Rs. 1,000 fine each, default 3 months additional rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction of all accused confirmed (judgment dated 17.09.2010)
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.34 for accused nos. 1, 2 and 4 (conviction upheld); accused no. 3 acquitted
neutral_facts: On 25 November 2003 the victim was found dead in the courtyard of a family house. The victim had been married into the household in July 2003. The prosecution case was that the step mother-in-law of the victim, who was annoyed with the victim over a domestic dispute, engaged three other persons to kill the victim. The only eyewitness was a thirteen-year-old domestic servant living in the house. According to the witness, one assailant held the victim while another stabbed the victim three to four times with a knife in the courtyard. The step mother-in-law was present in the passage, and a further person stood outside the house. After the assault, the assailants threatened the witness not to disclose anything. The witness was then taken to the terrace by the step mother-in-law and told to say that thieves had committed the crime. The step mother-in-law then began shouting and lay down near the victim. The victim's husband, returning from his clinic, found the servant weeping and the victim dead, and the step mother-in-law unconscious nearby. A First Information Report was lodged the same evening. Post-mortem examination recorded fourteen incised wounds, neurogenic and haemorrhagic shock as the cause of death, and a two-month pregnancy. Investigators seized a bloodstained knife, a hair found in the victim's grip, bloodstained cloth of the victim and of the step mother-in-law, and cement mortar. Three accused were arrested on 29 November 2003 and one on 22 December 2003. The witness identified the accused in test identification parades held within about a fortnight and four days of arrest, and identified them again in court.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by neurogenic and haemorrhagic shock; 14 incised wounds (including neck and chest), punctured lungs; victim was carrying a two-month fetus
number_of_offences: 1 offence (murder, s.302) charged with s.34 and s.120B as modes of liability; 1 finally upheld (for accused nos. 1, 2 and 4)
premeditation_planning: Yes. Court found the accused engaged paid killers with a single mission to kill the victim
motive: alleged: annoyance over domestic dispute with the victim; PW-1 deposed that accused no. 1 opposed the victim's marriage to her son because she wanted her daughter to marry him
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of child eyewitness PW-21; recovery of knife from accused no. 2 corroborating his account; identification parade and in-court identification of accused; hair found in deceased's grip; post-mortem findings
witness_credibility: PW-21 (child witness) found reliable: no reason to lie, no grudge or ulterior motive, presence in house natural; tutoring contention rejected as the period between arrest and identification parade was not inordinate
post_offence_conduct: Accused no. 1 asked the witness to conceal the truth and blame thieves; accused no. 2 threatened the witness not to disclose; all accused fled the scene
bail_history: Accused no. 3 was on bail (bail bonds cancelled on acquittal); otherwise not stated
trial_duration: offence: 25.11.2003; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 17.09.2010; Supreme Court: 21.08.2014
legal_representation: Appellants: P.C. Agrawala, Dr. Rajesh Pandey, Mahesh Pandey, Priyanka Pandey, Mridula Ray Bhardwaj, Revathy Raghavan, Vidya Dhar Gaur. Respondent (State): Atul Jha, Sandeep Jha, Dharmendra Kumar Sinha
investigation_status: FIR registered 25.11.2003; inquest, post-mortem, seizures and arrests completed; test identification parades held; charges framed and trial conducted with 32 prosecution witnesses
appeal_history: Trial court: all four convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 and s.120B, life imprisonment. High Court: conviction of all confirmed. Supreme Court: appeals of accused nos. 1, 2 and 4 dismissed; accused no. 3 acquitted
defence_argument: PW-21 was a tutored witness influenced by police, so his evidence needed close scrutiny and corroboration; delayed test identification made in-court identification unreliable; accused no. 3 merely stood outside and did not act as guard
legal_principle_applied: Child witness evidence assessed for reliability; corroboration by earlier identification is a safe rule of prudence where witness is a stranger to accused; common intention and conspiracy are matters of inference and benefit of doubt goes to accused
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: Baliya v. State of M.P. (2012) 9 SCC 696. Referred to: Budhsen v. State of UP (1970) 2 SCC 128; Suresh Sakharam Nangare v. State of Maharashtra (2012) 9 SCC 249; Jai Bhagwan v. State of Haryana AIR 1999 SC 1083; Ramashish Yadav v. State of Bihar (1999) 8 SCC 555. Distinguished: Subash and Shiv Kumar v. State of UP (1987) 3 SCC 331; Mohd. Abdul Hafeez v. State of Andhra Pradesh AIR 1983 SC 367
other_sentence_order: Accused no. 3's bail bonds cancelled and sureties discharged on acquittal
